Settings.title: Settings
Settings.lede: Durable preferences Momentum reads every time it plans for you.
Settings.noAthlete: We couldn't load your profile. Please sign out and try again.
Settings.languageNote: Applies to the app and Momentum right away. Sports terms like RPE and Zone 2 stay in English either way.
Settings.preferredNameNote: The name we send Momentum on your behalf. Leave it empty and we send none. Your account name is not sent — but anything you type yourself, in a note or a message, reaches Momentum as written.
Settings.raceTargetNote: The race you are training for. Everything in your plan is built backwards from it.
Settings.pastRacesNote: One per race. Your experience level follows this list.
Settings.racesNote: Everything in your plan is built backwards from your target. Other races before it are tune-ups — training days that happen to be races.
Settings.racesNone: No races yet. Add the one you are training for.
Settings.communicationStyleNote: How you like to be coached, in your own words. Momentum reads this to set its tone.
Settings.communicationStylePlaceholder: e.g. Direct and to the point — I don't need reassurance, just the plan.
Settings.weeklySessionDayNote: When Momentum opens next week's plan for you to look over.
Settings.fixedConstraintsNote: Momentum plans around these automatically, every week.
Settings.sharingIntro: {name} is your coach. What they can see is controlled here.
Settings.sharingAlwaysOnNote: Your calendar, sessions, statuses and move history. A coach who can't see the plan can't coach — sever the link instead if that's what you want.
Settings.sharingReportsLabel: Session Reflections, Check-in data & profile stats
Settings.sharingReportsNote: What you reported about your own body.
Settings.sharingTranscriptsNote: What you told the AI, unguarded. Off by default.
Settings.severConfirmBody: This cuts all access, including history, right away. {name} would need a new invite to relink.
Settings.severed: Link severed — you're back to training solo.
Settings.exportNote: A copy of everything this app holds about you — your plan, your sessions, your conversations with Momentum, your uploads and your profile.
Settings.deleteNote: Deletes your account and erases everything gathered from it. It happens immediately and cannot be undone.
Settings.deleteConfirmBody: This erases your training plan, every session and upload, your conversations with Momentum, your reflections, your equipment and your profile — and signs you out for good.
Settings.deleteConfirmIrreversible: It happens straight away. There is no undo, and no backup to restore from.
Settings.deleteError: That didn’t work. Nothing was deleted.
Settings.raceDistanceNote: The shape of your training week. Set it even if you have no race booked.
Settings.passwordChanged: Password changed. Other devices are signed out.
Settings.passwordMismatch: The two new passwords do not match.
Settings.passwordTooShort: A password needs at least {min} characters. This one has {actual}. Length is what keeps it safe — a few ordinary words work well.
Settings.passwordError: That did not work. Check the current password and try again.
Settings.passwordTooLong: That is longer than {max} characters. Shorten it a little.
Settings.passwordTooCommon: That is one of the first passwords anyone would try. Pick something else.
Settings.passwordPersonal: Leave your name and email out of it — anyone who has written to you knows both.

Glossary.title: Glossary
Glossary.subtitle: The training language in your plan and in Momentum’s messages

zone2.definition: Low-intensity aerobic effort where you can hold a conversation. The foundation of endurance training — develops fat oxidation and mitochondrial density over time.

vo2max.definition: The maximum rate at which your body can consume oxygen during exercise. A key predictor of endurance performance. Improved by high-intensity interval work.

lactateThreshold.definition: The intensity at which lactic acid accumulates in the blood faster than it can be cleared. Training at and around this zone raises the ceiling of sustainable effort.

ftp.definition: The highest average power you can sustain for approximately one hour on the bike. Used to set training zones for cycling.

hrv.definition: The variation in time between heartbeats. A higher HRV generally indicates better recovery. Useful for deciding when to push and when to back off.

tss.definition: A single number representing the training load of a session, combining intensity and duration. Used to track cumulative fatigue and fitness over time.

aerobicBase.definition: The accumulated low-intensity fitness that underlies all other training. A strong base allows higher intensity work to land on a stable foundation.

periodisation.definition: Structuring training into phases (base, build, peak, taper) so that stress and recovery are deliberately alternated to produce peak performance at the right time.

brick.definition: A workout combining two disciplines back-to-back — most commonly bike followed immediately by run. Trains your legs to adapt to the transition between disciplines.

interval.definition: Repeated hard efforts separated by recovery periods. Used to accumulate time at high intensity without excessive fatigue.

tempo.definition: A sustained effort at or near lactate threshold. Comfortably hard — you can speak in short sentences, not full paragraphs.

lsd.definition: A long session at Zone 2 intensity. Builds aerobic base, fat adaptation, and mental resilience without accumulating excessive fatigue.

fartlek.definition: Unstructured speed play within an otherwise easy session. Short bursts of effort at your own discretion — useful for breaking monotony while adding stimulus.

recovery.definition: A very easy, short effort designed to promote blood flow and aid recovery without adding meaningful training stress.

openWater.definition: A swim in natural water (lake, sea, river) as opposed to a pool. Involves sighting, drafting, and wetsuit adaptation — all race-specific skills.

transitions.definition: Transition zones. T1 is swim-to-bike; T2 is bike-to-run. Practice makes transitions faster and less stressful on race day.

ageGroup.definition: Your competitive category based on age, typically in 5-year bands. Most amateur triathletes compete in their AG rather than outright.

wetsuitLegal.definition: Water temperature is below the cutoff (typically 24.5°C / 76°F for non-elites) where wetsuits are permitted in competition.

dnf.definition: Did Not Finish / Did Not Start / Disqualified. Common race outcomes beyond a finish. A DNS is sometimes the smartest choice when injured.

drafting.definition: Swimming or cycling close behind another athlete to reduce drag. Legal in swim, banned on the bike in most amateur races, legal on the run.

specialNeeds.definition: A bag you can collect mid-race (usually mid-bike and mid-run) containing extra nutrition, a spare kit item, or anything you need for the second half.

ironman.definition: 3.8 km swim · 180 km bike · 42.2 km run. The full-distance triathlon. Also contested as 70.3 (half-iron): 1.9 km swim · 90 km bike · 21.1 km run.

FeedbackInterview.title: Feedback Interview
FeedbackInterview.intro: This is not Momentum. It is an interviewer, asking the questions the people building this app want answered — so it can follow up on what you say instead of leaving it at one line. Nothing you say here reaches Momentum.
FeedbackInterview.emptyBody: Anything: something that broke, something that annoyed you, something that worked. It will ask you to be specific.
FeedbackInterview.error: That did not go through. Your text is still here — try again, or use the box below.
FeedbackInterview.consentRequired: The interview needs AI consent, which you have not given. The box below works either way.
FeedbackInterview.fallbackBody: No conversation, no AI. This box works even when everything else does not.
FeedbackInterview.fallbackSent: Sent. Thank you — someone will read it.
FeedbackInterview.fallbackError: That did not save. Try again.

CoachDay.headline: Weekly planning day for {name}: {day}
CoachDay.intro: Training weeks for {name} start on {day}. Each week Momentum writes a draft of the next seven days. You see it first and can change it, and {name} decides whether to accept it.
CoachDay.nextDraft: You see the next draft {coachDate}; {name} sees it {athleteDate}.
CoachDay.confirmQuestion: Change the day to {day}? It applies from the next draft.
CoachDay.step1: Momentum drafts. On {coachDay}, the day before the planning day, it writes a proposal for {weekStart} – {weekEnd}, based on the race ({race}, {weeks, plural, =1 {1 week} other {# weeks}} out), the current Training Block ({block}), how last week went, and anything reported in the Check-in: an injury, an illness, or days marked unavailable.
CoachDay.step1NoRace: Momentum drafts. On {coachDay}, the day before the planning day, it writes a proposal for {weekStart} – {weekEnd}, based on how last week went and anything reported in the Check-in: an injury, an illness, or days marked unavailable.
CoachDay.step2: You look first. From {coachDay} the draft shows here, above the calendar. You can move, add or remove sessions before {name} sees it. Anything you change is shown to {name} as coming from you, by name.
CoachDay.step3: Then {name} decides. On {day} the draft appears on the Training Plan: accept it, discuss it with Momentum, which can then write a new draft, or leave it. Only an accepted week goes on the calendar; nothing is written to it automatically.
CoachDay.step4: If nobody acts, the draft stays a proposal. Nothing is scheduled until it is accepted, and it can still be accepted later in the week.
CoachDay.changing: Change the day only if the real training week starts on a different day. It applies from the next draft; the current proposal is not redrawn.

WeeklySessionDayLine.text: Your week is drafted every {coachDay} evening and shown to you {day}: accept it, discuss it, or leave it.
WeeklySessionDayLine.textLinked: Your week is prepared by {coach} and shown to you {day}: accept it, discuss it, or leave it.

WeekDraftReview.approvedChanged: Approved with your changes. The athlete will be told you shaped it.
